Hal Smith was born in Indianapolis on July 30, 1953. He grew up in California and started on the drums at age ten. Jake Hanna was an early teacher, but Hal learned his craft mostly from the recordings of Nick Fatool and Ben Pollack.

Hal has played behind many stars of mainstream jazz, including Bob Wilber, Doc Cheatham, Jim Cullum and Milt Hinton. Recordings for Arbors, Stomp Off and Good Time Jazz further enhanced his reputation and he expanded his skills into writing about jazz for The Mississippi Rag. Hal is the leader of the Road Runners with Rebecca Kilgore, and has toured Germany with his band Swing Cats.
Hal was interviewed on September 12, 1997 at the Allegheny Jazz Festival in Chautauqua, New York by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
We are talking today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive with band leader and drummer Hal Smith here in Chautauqua, New York. And thank you for joining us.
